description: Travel requires registering and waiting for a name to appear on a list published at intervals nobody controls. The waiting is measured in months.
energy_note: On a list, in a queue, for a gate that may not open.

aspect: EXAMPLE - $500 to skip the line, and it still did not work
description: Afaf al-Najar, 19, won a scholarship to study communications in Turkey, secured every document, and paid $500 to skip the long lines at Rafah. Palestinian border officials blocked her anyway - under the guardian rule.
money_note: Paid to bypass the queue. Non-refundable.
energy_note: Bought her way to the front, and was turned back at it.
notes: Two separate authorities stopped the same journey. See WOM-004.

aspect: The informal market is the actual system
description: Where a queue is long, scarce and opaque, brokerage appears. The fee is not a bribe to an individual so much as the market price of a public process that does not function.
energy_note: A tariff for something that should be free.

aspect: Which means mobility is means-tested by accident
description: Those who can pay travel. Those who cannot, wait. Nobody designed that as policy and it is the reliable outcome of every opaque queue.
energy_note: A border that quietly checks your bank balance.
